column1: # Machine-readable half of the skills-resync inventory: what each vendored skill was
# copied from, and the upstream tree hash it was copied at.
#   skill <TAB> source <TAB> subpath under the source <TAB> baseline (tree hash)
#         [<TAB> dest, relative to $SKILLS_DIR - omit for a skill, which vendors into its own name]
# A source is plugin@marketplace, or git+<repo>@<branch> (e.g.
# git+github.com/RisorseArtificiali/skills@main): a repo tracked at its branch tip - a plain
# repo, or a marketplace repo when only one skill of it is wanted - where this row is the whole
# spec and the branch tip is the upstream. resync.sh mirrors it at the tip and
# re-fetches on every --refresh - see SKILL.md "Upstream resolution".
# The optional 5th column is what lets a row vendor something that is not a skill. Only the shared
# `references/` tree uses it: the agent-skills bodies cite `../../references/<file>.md`, which from
# makes every one of those pointers resolve with no path edit and no patch. Relative on purpose:
# No version directory appears here on purpose. resync.sh resolves upstream from the
# marketplace clone under plugins/marketplaces/ (NOT the install cache, which is frozen for
# disabled plugins), following the source kind the marketplace catalog records - except for
# git+ rows, which bypass the catalog entirely. See SKILL.md "Upstream resolution".
# A new row is authored with `-` as its baseline: that is what marks it never-vendored, so --check
# reports it `unvendored` (APPLIABLE) and --apply performs the initial copy and writes the real
# hash. A missing directory under a *real* baseline is a copy that was lost, and stays BLOCKED.
# The baseline is a per-skill hash of the upstream skill directory, not a plugin commit sha:
# a commit elsewhere in the plugin no longer reads as "this skill moved". `--hash <dir>`
# prints one. It is rewritten by `resync.sh --apply` on every successful re-vendor.
# Do not hand-edit it: a baseline that lags reports upstream as moved when it has not.
# SKILL.md's L-flag index and RULINGS.md's full entries are the source of truth for *why* a
# row is here and which protected edits it carries. This file is the source of truth for
# The rows below ship the author's own vendored fleet as a worked example of the format,
# not configuration to reproduce. Point $INVENTORY at your own file (or start from an
# empty one) to manage a different set of vendored skills.
